answer.evidence: The bicycle is drawn in pure side profile: two wheels, a blue frame, and a basket facing right. The frame, wheels and fenders are all vertical silhouette with no horizontal surface. The rear carrier at rows 12-14 is only a thin band of about 2 rows, which counts as a rim. The basket at rows 3-14 is a front-facing mesh panel with groceries, so it counts as decor. No ellipse, roof, or edge line with eave shadow marks a top surface on the main body.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small bicycle with a basket and a rear-rack box. It reads clearly, and the measured facts are acceptable: 12 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge and 17-20 for the stall and well, 0% near-flat coverage, and 21% neutral dark edge pixels. The outline is partly tinted and partly dark grey-blue, with a few near-black frame pixels, so I rate it mixed. Shading is thinner than the references: the blue frame has about 3-4 steps (light blue, mid blue, dark, outline), the wheels are mostly dark ring with little tonal variation, and the basket and box are rendered with 2-3 greys. It has less per-material grain than the well and the stall, which carry 5-6 steps with per-stone and per-tile highlights. At this scale the 12 tones per tile is mid-range and not far below the references, but it is a small, thin object whose shading ramps are shallower than the Beodeul standard (about 5 steps). It is somewhat lower in richness, close to a careful-artist pass but not clearly equal. When in doubt, fail.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin, small object, a blue bicycle with a grey box on the rear rack, so I judged it by eye against the thin references (bench, lamp) as well as the measured facts. It measures 12 visible tones in a full tile, 0% near-flat coverage and 22 distinct colours. That is above the bench and lamp (about 14 colours each) and near the hedge (9 visible tones). It is below the stall (17) and well (20), but those are much larger and busier pieces. Only 21% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline mostly leans toward dark blue or grey-blue, the dark tone of the neighbouring material. The frame, wheels and box are separated by value, not by a uniform black line. The blue frame and grey box each show about 3-4 lightness steps, with highlights on the tyres and spoke or hub detail. That is a little short of Beodeul's 5-6, but there are no flat fills and no sticker look. A careful artist would accept it next to the bench and lamp without it looking thinner or flatter.
